doc.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview

title: Recording "JG" for Al Benson and Joe Segal's liner notes
summary: The Griffin band records the JG album in Al Benson's basement; Ware talks about the date and Joe Segal's notes.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Did that band ever make a record?

The band? Yes, it did. Only Clean Head wasn't on it. This was the band, you know, with Buddy Smith and Junior Mance and myself and Griff -- they had a disc jockey in Chicago, oh, he was very popular at that time. Al Benson. He come by the club and told Griff Red he wanted us to record. For him.

And so we said okay, and we go by the next day -- we go by Al's house, he had a home over on the South Side, in his basement, and he says he had a couple of tunes he's gonna fix. Al paid us off -- they made about $50 a piece -- and we recorded the next day after we rehearsed it, and I think they released that about '56 or '57 -- I think Al Benson had a tie up with the Chess Brothers, and I think it came out on Chess Records or Veejay -- I don't know which one -- but it was called "JG", and ...
Yeah, well, it was all souped up -- Chess or Argoyte or Veejay, I don't know which one, but....

Yeah. Well, that's the date we did. That was about in the winter of '54, I know, when we did that, because, see, I stayed with the man -- in fact, we had one of the swingingest bands on the South Side; we were working; this guy Ellsworth Ellis, Mason has the Flame down in Oakwood, as well as the Basin Street out there on 63rd and Cottage.

And we worked, maybe, a week out there -- then we replaced the band that he had down there at his other club. Dr. Joe Joe Adams had a little show, down at the Flame, and a cat named Benny Kelly -- a comedian -- had a show out there at Basin Street. And our show -- we had Clean Head singing with us, as well as Flynn, featuring the 4 pieces -- they had a thing where Cleanhead they played the opening tune with us on alto, but Griffin did most of the solo.
We did this record date, and it came out real nice. I think it's out of print now, though.
Do you want to talk about that date?
Segal wrote the liner notes. Joe, Seegle ...
Yeah, Joe was in on it -- quite a few of the names out there.
Well, he says he went back with Johnny Griffin from his teenage years.
